security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel context-switches between processes without saving/restoring the jvt CSR. A malicious process sets jvt.BASE to point to attacker-controlled memory, then yields the CPU. When the victim process executes cm.jalt or cm.jt, the hardware reads the jump target from the attacker's table via the stale jvt.BASE, redirecting the victim's control flow to an attacker-chosen address.
security_spec.summary: Zcmt introduces jvt CSR holding a jump-table base pointer; FreeBSD must save/restore jvt on context switch, validate jvt.BASE alignment (64-byte), enforce jvt.MODE=0, and in bhyve correctly trap or proxy guest jvt access via hstateen0.JVT — omission allows cross-process control-flow hijacking via stale jump-table pointer

findings.finding: The jvt CSR (address 0x017) is not defined in riscvreg.h. The CSR access macros (csr_read/csr_write/csr_swap) exist but no CSR_JVT constant is provided. This means no kernel code can read, write, or context-switch the jvt CSR.

spec_citations.excerpt: Table jump base vector and control register. Address: 0x017. Permissions: URW.
csr:jvt[] CSR adds architectural state to the system software context (such as an OS process), therefore must be saved/restored on context switches.

findings.finding: struct pcb has no pcb_jvt field to store the jvt CSR value across context switches. The PCB stores ra, sp, gp, tp, s[0-11], FPU registers, and fcsr, but no jvt state.

spec_citations.excerpt: csr:jvt[] CSR adds architectural state to the system software context (such as an OS process), therefore must be saved/restored on context switches.

findings.finding: cpu_switch() does not save/restore the jvt CSR. The context switch saves only ra, sp, s[0-11], and conditionally the FPU state. On hardware implementing Zcmt, leaving jvt un-switched allows a malicious process to set jvt.BASE to attacker-controlled memory; when the victim executes cm.jalt/cm.jt, the hardware fetches the jump target from the attacker's table via the stale jvt.BASE, redirecting victim control flow.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_switch)
    sd a1, PC_CURTHREAD(tp)
    ...
    sd ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
    sd sp, (PCB_SP)(x13)
    sd s0, (PCB_S + 0 * 8)(x13)
    ...
    /* no jvt CSR save/restore anywhere */

spec_citations.excerpt: csr:jvt[] CSR adds architectural state to the system software context (such as an OS process), therefore must be saved/restored on context switches.
insn:cm.jt[] reads an entry from the jump vector table in memory and jumps to the address that was read.

findings.finding: savectx() does not save the jvt CSR to the PCB. It saves ra, sp, tp, gp, s[0-11], and FPU state, but omits the jvt CSR. Any kernel path that uses savectx to snapshot thread state (e.g., crash dumps, ptrace) will silently lose the jvt value.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(savectx)
    sd ra, (PCB_RA)(a0)
    sd sp, (PCB_SP)(a0)
    sd tp, (PCB_TP)(a0)
    sd gp, (PCB_GP)(a0)
    /* s[0-11] saved, FPU saved, but no jvt */
    __fpe_state_save a0
    ret

findings.finding: cpu_throw() restores only ra, sp, s[0-11], and conditionally FPU state from the PCB. The jvt CSR is not restored. A newly-scheduled thread will inherit the previous thread's jvt value.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_throw)
    ...
    ld ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
    ld sp, (PCB_SP)(x13)
    ld s0, (PCB_S + 0 * 8)(x13)
    ...
    /* no jvt CSR restore */
    ret

findings.finding: exec_setregs() initializes a new process's register state but does not initialize the jvt CSR. A new process inheriting a stale jvt.BASE from its parent (via fork) could be exploited if the parent set jvt to point to attacker-controlled memory during its previous timeslice.

findings.finding: set_regs() (used by ptrace) copies register state into the thread's trapframe but has no jvt field in struct reg, so the jvt CSR cannot be read or written via ptrace debugging interfaces.
struct reg (the ptrace-visible register set) has no jvt field. This means debuggers and checkpoint/restore tools cannot inspect or modify the jvt CSR.
